note: Sensitive details such as addresses, device settings, control lists and security findings are left out. The experience and the results are not.

projects.title: Regional AI adoption
projects.summary: Taught around 300 employees to use Microsoft Copilot on their real work, then turned the best ideas from the business into working applications.
projects.challenge: AI tools only create value when people outside IT know how to use them on everyday tasks. Departments needed practical capability, and the business needed to know which ideas were worth building.
projects.responsibility: I led AI adoption across the region, including the training, the use-case initiative and delivery of the resulting applications.
decisions: Train on everyday tasks in each department rather than on the technology in the abstract.
Treat the training as the start of discovery, by collecting use cases from the people doing the work.
Carry the best findings through to working applications, so that ideas did not stop at a list.
Keep governance in view, informed by the ISO 42001 standard for AI management.
projects.solution: I delivered Microsoft Copilot training across multiple departments, then established an initiative to identify high-value AI use cases across the business and delivered working applications from the findings.
projects.result: Around 300 employees trained across departments, and working applications delivered from the use-case initiative.

projects.title: Aramco Cyber Security Certification
projects.status: Completed ahead of schedule, followed by a one-year device programme
projects.summary: Took the company through certification required by a key customer, ahead of a three-month deadline, then went further than asked and secured every connected device.
projects.challenge: A key customer required us to certify against its cybersecurity controls within three months, and failure could have stopped the business in the long term. Many technical safeguards were already in place. The harder gaps were in procedures, training and proving that every user had acknowledged the policy.
projects.responsibility: I was the principal lead for the certification, working with an authorised third party, departmental managers and the factory director.
decisions: Explain the business stakes to each department's management first, and secure the factory director's support.
Design the training myself around the customer's actual requirements, and deliver it across shifts so nobody was missed.
Automate policy acknowledgement with Microsoft automation and keep an auditable Excel record.
Go beyond the requirement: nobody asked us to inspect every PC and laptop, but I took the lead in doing so.
projects.solution: I closed the control gaps with the authorised third party, trained employees shift by shift, and sent each attendee the policy with an automated acknowledgement step. A twelve-month programme then followed to secure every device connected to the Saudi network.
projects.result: Certification achieved for Vallourec Saudi Arabia ahead of the expected schedule, then a completed year-long connected-device security programme. The certification belongs to the company, not to me personally.

projects.title: Mapping a whole plant's network
projects.summary: Recovered and documented the factory network from the machines on the floor up to core group switching, so incidents could be diagnosed from a desk.
projects.challenge: Every network incident meant walking the plant to trace connections by hand before the real investigation could even begin. No complete picture of the network existed, from the automation layer up to the core.
projects.responsibility: I decided to create the full picture and led the programme. I organised the site discovery and produced the documentation. The central network team configured the monitoring tool, and I gave them accurate site data for it.
decisions: Use a planned December shutdown for the site survey, to avoid disturbing production.
Bring in one contractor and walk the plant systematically, identifying switches, ports and connections, over about six days.
Draw the diagrams in a simple tool everyone could open and update: PowerPoint.
Feed the validated data to the network team so that it could become live monitoring maps in Zabbix.
projects.solution: Over a two-year programme delivered alongside routine operations, I recovered and defined the complete topology from the automation layer (IT/OT) through to core group switching, standardised interlinked site connectivity, and contributed architecture plans and recommendations. This work also supported the re-architecture of more than 100 Cisco and N-Tron switches to reduce latency.
projects.result: When a station later lost its network, the team used the diagrams and remote checks to identify the affected switch and go straight to it, instead of searching switch by switch. We can now also tell much faster whether a problem lies in the network, the PC or the machine.

projects.title: Digitalising a plant, from paper to live data
projects.summary: Moved shop-floor meetings, quality records, filing and procurement away from paper, and gave production management visibility of cycle times and shutdowns.
projects.challenge: Daily shop-floor meetings ran at three levels, from the floor to supervisors to department managers, and escalation relied on paper. Departments still used physical files, quality inspections were recorded on paper, and production management had limited visibility of where time was being lost.
projects.responsibility: The plant director asked me to find a solution for digitalising the shop-floor process. I gathered the requirements from each department, found the third-party provider who built the web application, supplied the hardware, and direct the wider digitalisation programme.
decisions: Meet the stakeholders in each department before choosing anything, so that the process reflected what they expected.
Bring a touchscreen experience onto the floor. Large screens were my proposal, chosen to suit the environment and the people using it.
Pilot in three buildings before asking the business to commit.
Keep IT requests traceable by logging each one raised on the floor in our global ticketing system, so that it was followed through to closure.
projects.solution: Shop-floor teams report on large touchscreens, with photos and named owners. I also moved departments from physical filing to SharePoint with automated workflows and digital signatures, introduced digital quality log sheets and digital procurement, and introduced cycle-time monitoring and shutdown analysis.
projects.result: Escalation became clearer, with email notifications and photo-based reporting, and paper use fell. After the pilot, the solution was adopted across the plant and grew to cover safety, maintenance, repair and IT requests. It was also demonstrated to process managers from other group entities, and production management gained visibility it previously lacked.

projects.title: Keeping the business running through COVID-19
projects.status: Completed; recognised with the Excellence Leader Award, 2020
projects.summary: With one technician, moved seven departments and about 100 people to remote work as part of the crisis cell.
projects.challenge: The pandemic meant people could no longer work from the plant and office as usual, and the business still had to run. There were two of us to do the work.
projects.responsibility: I was part of the crisis cell, and with one IT technician I carried out the move to remote work.
decisions: Prepare the whole working setup for each person: laptop, VPN, Teams training and a home office that worked.
Train people on Teams, so that the change worked in practice and not only on paper.
projects.solution: We prepared laptops and VPN access, trained people on Teams and set up remote offices for about 100 people across seven departments.
projects.result: The business kept running. I received the Excellence Leader Award in 2020 for performance through pandemic operations.

projects.title: Nine remote sites for more than 500 users
projects.status: Completed on time and within budget
projects.summary: Directed IT and construction contractors to stand up nine remote project sites, and resolved 79% of reported issues remotely.
projects.challenge: An Aramco contractor needed full infrastructure and IT assets at nine remote project sites, keeping more than 500 users connected.
projects.responsibility: I directed the IT and construction contractors, coordinated nine IT support and technical teams, and led vendor negotiation.
decisions: Resolve as much as possible remotely at first line, to avoid sending people to site.
Isolate two site networks, to strengthen security and keep daily operations going.
Audit sites every two to three months so that standards held after setup.
projects.solution: Each site received full infrastructure and IT assets. I ran remote services through the nine coordinated teams, negotiated laptops, servers and accessories, and worked with clients on the design of their site systems.
projects.result: Nine sites delivered for more than 500 users, on time and within budget, with 79% of reported technical issues resolved remotely.

projects.title: The machine that disappeared
projects.summary: A production application lost contact with a running machine. The first fix failed, so I went beyond my scope and found the cause with research and elimination.
projects.challenge: A production application could no longer communicate with a machine, even though the machine itself was running. The server side looked fine. Replacing the cable, the obvious first fix for equipment in heat and dust, did not solve it.
projects.responsibility: The fault sat on the automation side, outside my scope and my comfort zone. I took it on anyway.
decisions: Treat the failed first attempt as information, and reassess.
Eliminate each link in turn until the interface device between the machine and the switch was the only candidate left.
Use online research and AI tools together to find the manual and the correct configuration.
Finish with a lessons-learned session, so the fix did not live only in my head.
projects.solution: I tested the device away from the line, checked its settings and its physical configuration, researched the correct setup, and restored communication after several attempts.
projects.result: The machine showed up in the application again. I shared the standard with automation, maintenance and operational colleagues in a lessons-learned session. Why the setting changed in the first place remains unknown.

projects.title: Renewing ageing switches without disruption
projects.status: Completed; a routine repeated every two to three years
projects.summary: Spotted switches approaching the end of support in my inventory, made the risk case for budget, then replaced them building by building during shutdowns.
projects.challenge: The inventory I keep showed a group of switches about to become outdated, which would mean no support, no software updates and a direct security risk.
projects.responsibility: I raised the request, justified the budget, ordered the equipment, and planned and carried out the replacement with my team.
decisions: Make the budget case in terms of risk: no support, no updates, a security exposure.
Rehearse first. We built a replica of each live switch's configuration in the IT office and tested it.
Replace in stages, building by building and during shutdowns, with the new switch above the old one, moving ports one by one.
Verify at the application level, not just with a ping: test one device per VLAN and check that attendance machines appeared in their system.
projects.solution: Each switch was named, configured and tested before deployment, then confirmed online in Zabbix after replacement. We told each building about the change, updated the records with the new dates and versions, and arranged recycling through Sourcing.
projects.result: The replacements checked out and users reported no issues afterwards. No formal disruption metric was recorded.

projects.title: Moving identity and devices to the Microsoft cloud
projects.summary: Migrated on-premises Active Directory to Entra ID with Intune, lowering operating cost and centralising device compliance.
projects.challenge: On-premises Active Directory left endpoint management harder and more expensive than it needed to be.
projects.responsibility: I carried out the migration of user accounts and devices.
decisions: Use the move to centralise device compliance and application policy, not only to change where accounts live.
projects.solution: I migrated on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID with Intune, managing the work through to cutover and handover to support.
projects.result: Lower operating cost, simpler endpoint management, and centralised device compliance and application policy.

projects.title: A new regional office in six months
projects.summary: Opened a new office for the group, delivering full infrastructure readiness for employees end to end within six months.
projects.challenge: The group needed a new regional office with everything employees rely on already working.
projects.responsibility: I delivered the office's IT infrastructure end to end.
decisions: Run it as a full project: scope, resources, cost, risk, testing, cutover and handover.
projects.solution: I took the work from scope and planning through implementation and testing, to handover to support.
projects.result: Full infrastructure readiness, delivered within six months.

projects.title: NDT production-line replacement
projects.summary: Adapted the IT tracking systems for machines inside the production line through each phase of a major equipment changeover.
projects.challenge: Replacing inspection equipment on a live production line changes the process at every phase, and the digital tracking has to keep up at each step.
projects.responsibility: I supported the project on the IT side, directing the IT tracking systems for the production machines.
decisions: Work phase by phase, so process changes were reflected digitally as each stage went live.
projects.solution: I adapted the production tracking systems and accommodated process changes digitally through each phase of the replacement.
projects.result: Product tracking kept pace with the process through each phase of the changeover.

projects.title: Regaining control of more than 1,000 devices
projects.summary: Initiated departmental IT procedures, unified asset models with registered lifespans, and brought the estate under control.
projects.challenge: Control of the device estate across head office and remote sites needed to be regained, with no unified standards for models or lifespans.
projects.responsibility: I initiated and led the work as Head of IT.
decisions: Start from procedures and standards for all departments, then unify asset models and types, and register a lifespan for each.
projects.solution: Over a one-year project I put procedures and standards in place for every department, and registered servers, switches, firewalls, laptops, desktops and mobiles.
projects.result: More than 1,000 devices brought back under control, with unified models and registered lifespans.

projects.title: QR-code processing application
projects.summary: Built an automated QR-code scanning and processing system with an interactive GUI, reducing manual handling errors.
decisions: Automate the scanning and processing, and give users a simple interactive interface.
projects.solution: An automated QR-code processing application with an interactive GUI.

projects.title: Exchange Online migration
projects.summary: Migrated user accounts and email for a 699-user organisation to Microsoft Exchange Online with zero downtime.

projects.title: Biometric attendance across every site
projects.summary: Deployed biometric attendance systems and tracking software at every site, improving payroll accuracy.

projects.title: Connected-device security programme
projects.summary: Secured every device connected to the Saudi network over a twelve-month programme following certification.

projects.title: Operator learning through QR codes
projects.summary: Printed guides at production stations with QR codes linking to short videos, giving operators repeatable help across shifts.

projects.title: HR and IT onboarding and offboarding
projects.summary: A documented draft process for approved requests, device preparation, inventory, asset returns, account deactivation and SIM reconciliation.

projects.title: Account and licence hygiene
projects.summary: Reviewed inactive accounts with HR and set up a recurring monthly review to keep accounts clean and licences well used.

projects.title: Site IT assessments
projects.summary: Visited sites and wrote assessments covering equipment, tested connectivity options, support model and open items, so that decisions rested on evidence.

projects.title: Server estate with backup and recovery
projects.summary: Deployed more than 20 physical and virtual servers with backup and disaster recovery, enabling rapid restoration.

projects.title: Supplier-integrated product tracking
projects.summary: Kept real-time tracking and Optimised Material Management (PSI) systems accurate across integrated applications and supplier interfaces.

personal.title: RFQ Master
personal.status: Live platform, preparing for a controlled launch
personal.role: Product owner directing development, user experience and AI-assisted improvement
personal.summary: A business procurement platform connecting buyers and suppliers through requests for quotation, comparison, negotiation and purchase orders. I shape the requirements and user journeys, coordinate implementation, and use AI-assisted development and review to improve it.
decisions: Keep the underlying procurement workflow stable while improving the experience.
Define distinct buyer, supplier and administrator journeys.
Check improvements in isolation before a controlled release.
Treat recovery and operational readiness as part of delivery.
personal.note: The technologies describe the implementation environment. My role is product ownership and AI-assisted delivery.

personal.title: Pixel Zone: an AI Arabic newsroom
personal.status: Working prototypes, human-reviewed, automatic publishing paused
personal.role: Concept, editorial requirements, workflow direction, visual review and AI-assisted development
personal.summary: An experiment in turning sourced news into clear Arabic editorial packages, combining source discovery, structured AI editing, visual production and human review, with a companion mobile app for publishing.
decisions: Keep source links and distinguish between levels of source confidence.
Use structured model outputs and deterministic checks.
Design separately for each publishing format.
Keep a human approval step, and make publication state explicit.
contributions: Local editorial memory learned from skip decisions
personal.note: This is not a verified news service. It keeps source references but does not independently establish truth or image rights.

personal.title: Mansour's Wallet
personal.status: Working Android app, public test build
personal.role: Concept, direction, hands-on testing and AI-assisted delivery
personal.summary: An offline-capable card collection app that turns a physical collection into a searchable digital library and an interactive map. I direct the experience, test the results, and turn detailed feedback into successive working releases.
decisions: Confirm identification before saving.
Keep original photos available for review.
Keep every card accessible, even when details are unknown.
Distinguish real reference data from estimates.
Protect user data across updates and restores.
contributions: Camera, gallery, manual and catalogue entry
personal.note: Testing continues. Condition checks are experimental and reviewed by the user.

personal.title: Multi-agent research platform
personal.status: Design and specification stage, not built
personal.summary: A concept for turning an initial idea into a structured, testable hypothesis, comparing independent AI analyses and keeping an evidence trail, with people in control of the decision rules and paper-only testing.
decisions: Separate hypothesis building, research, counter-analysis and adjudication.
Use schema-validated outputs and source-linked claims.
Keep human control of how factors are weighted.
Give models no authority to execute anything.
personal.note: A detailed specification only. It has no results or returns to report.

personal.title: Atlantis: an interactive design vision
personal.role: Creative direction and AI-assisted interaction refinement
personal.summary: A visual exploration of an imagined villa, presented through guided and self-directed photographic discovery, with responsive galleries and day and night comparisons.
decisions: Offer both a guided tour and category browsing.
Provide ordinary navigation that works without scripts.
Present the work explicitly as a design concept.
personal.note: A design concept, not a built property or real-estate offer.

personal.title: Hospital database system
personal.role: Co-author of a two-student database and interface project
personal.summary: A university project modelling doctors, patients, medicines and appointments, and connecting a Java interface to a relational database.
decisions: Separate database and interface concerns.
Represent the core entities and their relationships.
Resolve date-type mismatches between Java and the database.
personal.note: A student project, not deployed in a clinical setting.
